newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Algerian natural gas supplies reach Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Algerian natural gas supplies reach Portugal.

text.p: Natural gas sent down a $1.88 billion pipeline from Algeria has reached Portugal on schedule and engineering tests and cleaning operations were taking place before distribution, a source involved in the process said.
Construction of the pipeline, which sends natural gas from Algeria to Portugal via Morocco and Spain, was completed last November.

"The first supplies of natural gas should be delivered by Transgas to regional distributors and industrial companies in Portugal from March 1, 1997," the source, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
State company Transgas expects to supply the Tapada power plant in northern Portugal, described as the most advanced being built in Europe, in October 1997, the source added.

The 1,000 MW power plant at Tapada do Outeiro, 18 km (11 miles) southeast of Oporto, will supply 20 percent of Portugal's electricity and may export energy to Spain after commercial operations start in March 1998.

Transgas has begun a study into the possibility of building a natural gas terminal in the western ports of Sines or Setubal to reduce the risks of the Portuguese natural gas system depending exclusively on supplies from Algeria, the source said.
